objective: Publish the readiness and phase-gate artifact sets atomically: render the report/status JSON, the generated markdown page, the release-notes block and the English and Chinese README blocks into a staging area, verify them byte for byte, and only then rename the whole set into place, so an interrupted generation leaves every target byte-identical to its pre-run state instead of a new report beside old generated views.
decision_supported: Whether an operator, a release job or a CI gate may treat the committed readiness and phase-gate artifacts as one coherent generation, instead of having to rerun the gate to discover whether the checkout holds a mixed set that is indistinguishable from a hand-edited artifact.
acceptance: readiness_report.py::write_outputs and phase_gates.py::write_outputs render every output into a hidden staging directory beside its target, re-read and compare each staged file byte for byte, and only then rename the set into place, so a simulated failure after the first write leaves every target byte-identical to its pre-run state

there is no sequential fallback: when staging cannot be created, or any staging write or verification fails, the writer raises a named GeneratedArtifactSetError identifying the artifact set and the reason, and publishes nothing
a failure during the renames restores every target already replaced from the bytes it held before the run, so a torn set is not left on disk

a successful run updates the JSON artifact, the markdown page, the release-notes block and both README blocks as one set, and the published content is byte-identical to what the previous sequential writer produced (block splicing behaviour is preserved unchanged)
generation of the same targets is serialised by an advisory lock under the gitignored build/locks directory, so two concurrent generations cannot interleave their files

the writers keep the committed generated_at and source_commit when a regeneration reproduces every other field, so regenerating an up-to-date checkout rewrites no tracked artifact; a run that changes a stated field republishes the whole set with fresh stamps
check_readiness_report.py and check_phase_gates.py still pass on the committed artifacts and additionally refuse a checkout left with staging residue from an interrupted generation
the change is confined to generator write behaviour: no report content, evidence vocabulary, public schema, runtime or control path changes, and no new runtime dependency is added
commands: python3 -m ruff check tools/scripts/readiness_report.py tools/scripts/phase_gates.py tools/scripts/check_readiness_report.py tools/scripts/check_phase_gates.py tests/unit/test_readiness_report.py tests/unit/test_phase_gates.py

python3 -m ruff format --check tools/scripts/readiness_report.py tools/scripts/phase_gates.py tools/scripts/check_readiness_report.py tools/scripts/check_phase_gates.py tests/unit/test_readiness_report.py tests/unit/test_phase_gates.py
evidence: pytest transcript for tests/unit/test_readiness_report.py and tests/unit/test_phase_gates.py with the passed count
the mid-write interruption test: an injected failure after the first staged write, asserting every target is byte-identical to its pre-run snapshot and no staging residue remains
the successful-replacement test: the JSON artifact, the page, the release-notes block and both README blocks all published as one set with the expected bytes
the serialisation test: three concurrent generations of the same targets whose publish intervals never overlap, leaving one coherent set
the unchanged-run evidence: make readiness-report-check and make phase-gates-check leave git status clean on a checkout whose inputs did not change
ruff check and ruff format output for every changed Python file, and the task-packet boundary check output
stop_conditions: the change would require a new runtime dependency or a database to stage or publish the set
the change would require editing interfaces/, libs/contracts/, a schema or a Pydantic model
the change would alter generated artifact content or the evidence vocabulary rather than only how it is published
the change would require a physical, Gazebo or HIL claim, or an executed external run
the change would rewrite tracked artifacts purely to refresh a timestamp on a checkout whose inputs did not change
a required modification falls outside allowed_paths
data_classification: public repository source, documentation and committed generated artifacts; no secrets, personal data, credentials or physical measurement data
model_policy: AI may write the staging/publish policy, the two generators, the two gates, the tests and the operating notes; a named human Owner accepts the staging/publish policy and owns the release decision the artifacts inform
risks_and_fallbacks: staging beside the target could leave residue if the process is killed; fallback is that the staging directory is removed on every observable failure, and both gates report residue as a finding and refuse to certify the set
a rename failure midway could leave a mixed set; fallback is that the writer restores every target already replaced from its pre-run bytes and reports the rollback in the named error
the lock files could dirty the checkout they are meant to protect; fallback is that they live under the gitignored build/locks directory and never inside the artifacts

keeping the committed stamps when nothing else changed could hide a real regeneration; fallback is that the gate still compares every field the document states, so a changed input fails until the set is republished with fresh stamps

generated_at could be read as evidence of when the software was ready; fallback is that the document's own edit policy states only generated_at and source_commit change without a change of inputs, and the gate compares every other field
rollback is a revert of this commit; the change is confined to how the existing artifacts are written and no fixture, manifest, schema or runtime path changes
